_doc: Hot-path ids for `// perf-hot: <budget> <path-id>` markers (plans/cmux-next/codebase-health.md section 6). scripts/cmux-next/guardrails.py warns when a push changes a marked function and names the bench here. Run it yourself on the fleet (nx-remote --needs gui), light and STRESS (perf-lead-brief), before and after; never add it to CI.

terminal-host-output.what: one PTY read in a terminal host (terminal_host_runtime/shared): publish_pty_frame makes the one shared Output frame, and the client writer sends the frames queued at each wake in one vectored write
terminal-host-output.bench: cmux-tui/scripts/bench-terminal-perf.py (throughput and busy sections: MB/s and host CPU %), on the bench Mac with cmux-tui and cmux-tui-host built

chats-window-query.what: one keystroke on the command palette's chats page: acpmux's query window (chats/window.rs ranked_rows) ranks every chat's title, then searches the held text of every chat for the words (chats/text.rs ChatText::search, one pass, its answer kept until the text changes) and builds the snippets of the rows it shows
chats-window-query.bench: cargo test -p acpmux --lib chats::text::tests::search_bench -- --ignored --nocapture (2,000 chats; prints p50/p95/max per keystroke)

daemon-request.what: the app's daemon-request probe on every request to the daemon (DaemonRequestLatency.record: one bucket lookup and three relaxed atomics)
daemon-request.bench: scripts/cmux-next/austins-day (app_requests: the probe's own p99 under 80 agents)

cef-host-input.what: one input event forwarded to the Chromium host app (prototype, browserHost.helperPrototype): encode and one non-blocking write

key-dispatch.what: every key-down: shortcut table, chord tracker, focus routing

terminal-key.what: terminal key to committed frame (input write, echo, parse, draw)

terminal-output-scan.what: the byte scanners every terminal output chunk runs in the host and in the daemon mirror: the title tracker (terminal_title.rs TitleTracker::rewrite), the OSC metadata collector (terminal_metadata.rs OscCollector::observe) and the prompt mark search (prompt_mode_reset.rs); each jumps over the bytes no state can change on
terminal-output-scan.bench: cargo test -p cmux-tui-core --release --lib terminal_output_scan_bench -- --ignored --nocapture (64 KiB colored log and box-drawing TUI output; prints ns per byte, jumping scan and byte-at-a-time reference)

palette-key.what: Command Palette open and each query key to its first painted frame

omnibar-key.bench: scripts/cmux-next/omnibar-click-bench.py (focus), then bench-typing.py with the omnibar focused

motion-frame.bench: scripts/measure/split-spring.sh --suite=pane-bench (PaneMotionBench, PaneMotionWorkTests), then pane-perf-terminal.py and anim-perf-terminal.py (panes.* rows, with and without Chromium, light and --layouts stress)

frame-tick.what: the per-display-frame delivery to every active frame client

drag-frame.what: one tab, pane or column drag frame (ghost, autoscroll, hit test)

launch-first-frame.what: each visible pane at launch or reopen, before the window's first frame: a terminal's saved frame shown ahead of its surface (one layer, decoded off the main thread)
launch-first-frame.bench: scripts/cmux-next/bench-startup.py (launch.visible_terminals_drawn) and the REOPEN VIDEO film (reopen_judge.py)

pane-verb-turn.what: Toggle Pane Zoom and Swap Pane, from the action's handler to the layout the window shows: one store intent, then one layout apply per window that shows the workspace, all in the input's turn (no daemon wait)
pane-verb-turn.bench: PaneVerbsKeyTurnTests and PaneLayoutIntentTests (the change is in the layout model when the handler returns; the daemon's echo applies no layout), then scripts/cmux-next/pane-perf-terminal.py --actions zoom

cef-geometry.what: Chromium page geometry, clip and occlusion updates
cef-geometry.bench: scripts/cmux-next/pane-perf-terminal.py with a Chromium page (debug.cef geometry posts per frame)

window-resize-step.what: one step of a live window resize (a person drags an edge): AppKit lays the window's view tree out inside setFrame, so every chrome view's layout() runs once per step and all of them share one refresh. Work that does not depend on the new size (rebuilding tooltips or accessibility elements, drawing a view that only moved) does not belong in it.
window-resize-step.bench: swift test --filter WindowResizeWorkPerStepTests with CMUX_TEST_SESSION_SIZES=large,real (prints WORK case=window-resize per session size: layout calls per step and per class); frame times by a real corner drag (CuaDriver, 1280x800 to 1040x640) with the same drag on Chrome as the reference: window-edge intervals from debug.motion record_start, main-thread time from debug.frames

cmd-tab.what: app activation (Cmd-Tab back): become/resign key notices to committed frame, including the hover refresh

new-tab.what: new terminal or Chromium tab to its first frame

main-task-record.what: every scheduled main-thread task's always-on per-owner time record (MainTaskTimes.record from MainFrameBudget.run: the owner's slot lookup, one bucket and a few stores; debug.main_budget's owners)
main-task-record.bench: CMUX_MAIN_TASK_RECORD_BENCH=1 swift test -c release --filter MainTaskRecordBench (ns per task for owners interned first, after 1500 names, and 400 owners in turn)

action-budget.what: every action run's always-on budget record: two clock reads and one ring-slot write (ActionBudgetMonitor.record)
action-budget.bench: CMUX_ACTION_BUDGET_BENCH=1 swift test -c release --filter ActionBudgetMonitorBench (ns per run and per batch), on macOS 26 and 27

chats-window-diff.what: one acpmux chats window message on the main actor: AcpmuxChatWindows.apply walks the window's keys (20 for the sidebar history, 24 for New Tab cards, a palette page), never acpmux's index. acpmux holds the index (3,000 chats in the test) and sends only the window's changed rows.
chats-window-diff.bench: ChatsWindowMainThreadTests (a 20-row window over a 3,000-chat index that stays in acpmux: one changed chat is one row in the message and the window's keys on main) on the fleet, and the debug hang monitor (debug.hangs) on a many-chat load

acpmux-wait-wake.what: one acpmux hub record seen by an open _acpmux/wait: the session filter and the streamed-chunk skip; a chunk never evaluates the wait's rows
acpmux-wait-wake.bench: cmux-tui-rust-check.sh test a_streamed_token_does_not_evaluate_an_open_wait (WAIT-STREAM line: evaluations per 500 tokens), then scripts/measure/acpmux-overhead.sh bench=daemon (STRESS token to client) on the fleet
acpmux-wait-wake.owner: PL-acpmux (HOT PATH AUDIT area F: hpa-stream)

home-stream-token.what: one streamed token of a Chief reply on the main thread: HomeLiveBook append, publishLive of that conversation, and each open Home view's store observation (whole-message views are not woken by a talk token)
home-stream-token.bench: HomeWholeMessageTokenCostTests (HOMETOKEN lines: ms per token, wakes and passes, 1 and 4 views, 2,000 messages) and HomeStreamingPerfTests (streaming mode), run on the fleet (package-test-lane.sh suite Packages/Shared/CmuxMessagesLab)

acpmux-token-fanout.what: one streamed token to one attached acpmux connection: the shared session/update line enqueued (one copy into the connection's queue); the line is built once per record
acpmux-token-fanout.bench: cmux-tui-rust-check.sh test a_streamed_tokens_line_is_built_once_for_every_attached_connection (FANOUT-ENCODE line), then scripts/measure/acpmux-overhead.sh bench=daemon (STRESS token to client, 2 clients) on the fleet
acpmux-token-fanout.owner: PL-acpmux (HOT PATH AUDIT area F: hpa-stream)

composer-draft-typing.what: one key in the agent chat composer: the prompt's markdown written from each top-level block's kept markdown (MarkdownField.tsx blockwiseMarkdown), so only the block the key changed is serialized
composer-draft-typing.bench: CMUX_LATENCY_DRAFTS=1 bun webviews/scripts/latency/run.ts --page "chat draft typing" (10k and 200k-character drafts, 3,000-turn chat)

session-list-change.what: one session_changed while the agent pane is open (direct.ts sessionChanged, then App's per-snapshot projections of snapshot.sessions: hover info, sub-session store, Waiting on you, folders). Its cost must not grow with the number of listed sessions.
session-list-change.bench: webviews/bench/update-one.bench.ts (update_one.<surface>.<kind>.n100|n1000|n3000 and .growth; cmux-ci test -- bun bench/update-one.bench.ts)

workspace-list-change.what: one workspace made or closed (the daemon's workspace-added / workspace-closed event, DaemonStore.drain): the observers it wakes, the membership reconcile, the placement and the sidebar sections pass. Its main-thread cost must not grow with the number of workspaces of the session (826 in the person's session, 60 in the `large` one).
workspace-list-change.bench: count: CMUX_TEST_SESSION_SIZES=large,real swift test --filter WorkspaceListChangeWakeTests (on a build mini); the list's scroll rule (ListViewportChange, SidebarLayout.viewportPositions): swift test --filter "SidebarRowChangeScrollTests|SidebarViewportRuleEqualityTests" (viewport_rows per change at 60 and 826 rows); time: session_real.py launch ... --steps "agents,wait:6,clients:13,wait:8,map:--runs 20" at 60 and 826, rows new workspace and workspace close (main-thread gap and stalls per action)

workspace-placement.what: one new workspace put at its sidebar slot once the daemon reports it (WindowManager.applyPendingPlacements -> SidebarBridge.place): the rows it maps from their stores. It maps the new row only, at 60 workspaces as at 826. Still O(session) per placement and not covered by this budget: the two rows passes (structure walk and SidebarModel.setSections), the document projection in the Rust mirror, and the slot rule's copy of every row (SidebarSection.withoutPlaceholders, counted as slot_rows).
workspace-placement.bench: count: CMUX_TEST_SESSION_SIZES=large,real swift test --filter WorkspacePlacementCostTests (on a build mini; rows_made, doc_reshows, project, slot_rows per placement)

command-stats.what: the session daemon's count of one request by command name and client kind (diagnostics/command_stats.rs: CommandStats::start, start_line, Cell::record; server/connection_frame.rs handle_connection_frame and handle_request_with_cancellation): three clock reads, one probe of a fixed table, four relaxed atomic updates, no lock, no allocation after the first request of a name
command-stats.bench: cargo test --release -p cmux-tui-core --lib bench_command_stats_cost_per_request -- --ignored --nocapture (in cmux-tui, on a build mini; prints COMMAND-STATS-BENCH with ping_with_ns, ping_without_ns and added_ns for 1 000 000 ping requests, same binary)
